$comment: CANONICAL INTENT INDICATORS — Vietnamese surface cues for classifying what the user is asking for, shared by the Java and Python resolvers. Intent decides whether a colour may be produced at all: answering 'dấu hiệu cảnh báo thai kỳ là gì?' with RED would report an encyclopaedia question as an assessment of the person asking. No LLM contributes to this file.

matchingRules.$comment: Evaluated in the declared precedence order; the first intent whose cues match wins. FOLLOW_UP_ANSWER is decided structurally (an option code was submitted), never by phrase matching.

sourceLookup.$comment: Asking where information came from. Must not run symptom rules.

generalHealthInformation.$comment: Asking what something IS, in general. The giveaway is an interrogative about a category rather than a report about the speaker's own body.

emergencyHelp.$comment: An explicit call for urgent help. This does NOT itself decide RED — the Global Safety Gate does. It only routes and prioritises.

symptomTriage.$comment: A first-person report of a current symptom. Deliberately broad: when a message reports a symptom AND asks a general question, the symptom report wins, because leaving a real symptom untriaged is the worse error. Short words whose accent-stripped form collides with a different word are matched WITH accents and whole-word only — 'dấu' (sign) folds to the same string as 'đau' (pain), so folded matching would read 'dấu hiệu cảnh báo là gì?' as a pain report.

accentSensitiveMarkers.$comment: Matched against the accented, lowercased text with whole-word boundaries.

outOfScopeRequest.$comment: Explicitly asking for something CareBridge does not do. Kept narrow: this is about the REQUEST, not about the clinical scope of a complaint (that is scopeStatus).
